topic: Pigeons, a hiss, and the Big Bang's echo (1960s)
claim: Bell Labs' Penzias and Wilson tried to remove a background hiss from their Holmdel horn antenna, even trapping nesting pigeons and cleaning out droppings; it proved to be the cosmic microwave background (about 3 K), the Big Bang's afterglow, and won them the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics.

beats.vo: They blamed pigeons. It was the Big Bang's echo.
In the 1960s, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson aimed a giant horn antenna at space, in New Jersey.
But a faint hiss came from every direction. Pigeons were nesting inside, so they trapped the birds and scrubbed out the droppings. The hiss stayed.
After a year, the noise was still there: microwaves at about three degrees above absolute zero. Princeton's Robert Dicke explained it: the afterglow of the Big Bang.
Penzias and Wilson won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics. The static was a signal from the early universe.
